rationale: C05 plausibly supplied a material administrative template: both directives concern transferring United States agricultural commodities to a named foreign country, assign operational authority to the foreign-aid director, and reserve negotiation of the recipient-country agreement to the Secretary of State. The child adapts this machinery from Pakistan wheat assistance to Bolivian emergency relief, adding a presidential quantity determination and more detailed allocation of delivery costs and program administration. C20 supplies the broader FOA/State division of responsibility and is a strong secondary source, while C17 contains analogous transfer-agreement-and-consultation machinery but for vessels rather than relief commodities.

shared_material.child_excerpt: agricultural commodities shall be made available out of the stocks of the Commodity Credit Corporation and transferred to meet the urgent relief requirements of Bolivia
shared_material.parent_excerpt: functions vested in the President by the Act of June 25, 1953, entitled "An Act to provide for the transfer of price-support wheat to Pakistan"
shared_material.explanation: Both directives implement a transfer of federally controlled agricultural commodities to a specified foreign government for assistance.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Arrangements for the operations of this relief program ... shall be the responsibility of the Director of the Foreign Operations Administration
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Director for Mutual Security is hereby designated and empowered to perform ... the functions vested in the President
shared_material.explanation: Both place implementation of the commodity-transfer program with the principal foreign-assistance director; the child updates the office to the Foreign Operations Administration.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Secretary of State ... shall conclude a bilateral agreement with the Government of Bolivia
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of State is hereby designated and empowered to negotiate and enter into an agreement with Pakistan
shared_material.explanation: This is the clearest parallel operative mechanism: the foreign-aid director administers the assistance while the Secretary of State handles the bilateral agreement with the recipient country.
